title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: How can you verify that the cabin door latch assembly is correctly aligned and functioning properly after adjustments?
answer: Do the adjustment of the latch assembly. . (1) Make sure the cabin door is installed and fitted to the fuselage before the adjustment/test can be done. (2) Make sure the cabin door latch is in the OPEN position before the adjustment/test can be done. (3) Make sure the door latch operates smoothly and freely. (4)  Make sure the bolt or pull bar are not filed, ground, or sanded in any way. NOTE:  A noise can be heard when the inside handle is pushed down. It is recommended that the outside door handle be flush with the door skin, although the noise is heard. (5) Install shims to adjust the striker plate forward to give a minimal clearance between the bolt and the striker plate. NOTE:  This adjustment will make sure that the pushrod will engage the latch catch. It will also make sure the exterior handle will stay open until the door is closed again when the door is opened from the outside. (6) Install shims as necessary below the actuator on the cover assembly. NOTE:  If the cabin door is too far forward, the door latch will not operate correctly because the latch assembly pushrod will not cause the bolt to move. (7) Close the cabin door from inside the airplane. (8) Make sure the exterior handle is flush with the door skin when you close the door. (a) If the exterior handle is not flush with the door skin when the door is closed, adjust the push-pull rod out. 1  Remove the screws and the nuts that attach the base plate to the door. 2  Remove the smaller end of the push-pull rod and turn it 180 degrees. 3  Install the screws and nuts that attach the base plate. (9) Do a check for slippage between the cable casing and the clamps that attach the cable.  Install the cotter pin in the clevis pin.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What is the recommended procedure for preparing the door surface before applying adhesive during cabin door weatherstrip installation?
answer: Cabin Door Weatherstrip Removal . (1)  Use a nonmetallic scraper to remove the weatherstrip and adhesive from the door assembly. (2)  Use solvent to remove all remaining adhesive from the door surface.Cabin Door Weatherstrip Installation . (1)  Cut the new weatherstrip to the correct length with the used weatherstrip as a template. (2)  Cut a small notch in the butt ends of the new weatherstrip to let water drain. (3)  Put the weatherstrip in position with the notches at the door low point. (4)  Apply a thin, smooth layer of EC-1300L, or equivalent adhesive to the two surfaces. (5)  Let the adhesive dry until it is tacky. (6)  Push the weatherstrip in position. (7)  Do not stretch the weatherstrip around the door corners.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the key steps to ensure the cabin door latch operates freely and correctly after completing the cable assembly rigging process?
answer: Do the Cabin Door Latch Cable Assembly Rigging . Attach the clamp and the nut to the cable so it aligns with the 0.193 inch  diameter hole Make sure the door latch is open. Cut the casing of the cable assembly approximately two inches  from the clamp bolt on Put the core of the cable through the clamp. Pull the core of the cable through the clamp bolt so the pin extends approximately 0.125 inch  from the door pan contour. Cut the core of the cable approximately one inch  forward of the push rod clamp. Attach the two nuts to the push rod clamp bolt. Make sure the latch operates freely. If the latch binds up and will not operate freely, remove the cable core from the clamp and Do a check of the cable for possible adjustments that will make the latch operate correctly.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the detailed steps required to remove and reinstall the cabin door lock assembly, including how to access the interior panels and reassemble the surrounding components?
answer: Cabin Door Lock Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the lower door accent panel and main door panel to get access to the cabin door lock assembly. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices. (2) Remove the armrest door plugs, door panel insert at the armrest, armrest, door handle and cover plate from the door to get access to the cabin door lock assembly. (3) Remove the nut and washer. (4)  Remove the cabin door lock assembly.Cabin Door Lock Assembly Installation . (1) Put the cabin door lock assembly in position. (2) Install the washer and nut. (3) Install the armrest door plugs, door panel insert at the armrest, armrest, door handle and cover plate. (4)  Install the lower door accent panel and main door panel. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What is the proper sequence for attaching the pushrod assembly to the pull bar, ensuring the latch is in the closed position, and adjusting the push-pull rod to require 6 to 12 pounds of force during cabin door inside handle rigging?
answer: Do the Cabin Door Inside Handle Rigging . (1) Attach the pushrod assembly to the pull bar and attach it with the pin while the latch is attached to the door pan. (2)  Do not install the cotter pin. (3)  Make sure the latch is in the closed position. (4)  Remove the pin that connects the push-pull rod to the latch base assembly. (5) Adjust the rod so a load of 6 to 12 pounds  is necessary at the end of the inner handle to move it from the closed position to the over center position. NOTE:  The rod can be turned in or out 180 degree to make the applicable adjustments. NOTE:  The rod must be attached to the latch assembly before the cabin door inside handle rigging can be done.

question: What are the detailed procedures for removing and reinstalling the baggage door lock assembly, including the steps to secure the anti-rotational washer?
answer: Baggage Door Lock Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the baggage door panel to get access to the lock assembly of the baggage door. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices. (2) Remove the 0.75-inch hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. (3) Remove the lock assembly from the door.Baggage Door Lock Assembly Installation . (1) Put the baggage door lock assembly in position on the baggage door. (2) Install the 0.75-inch hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. Make sure that the anti-rotational washer is installed under the 0.75-inch hex nut. (3) Torque the nut. (4) Bend the applicable tab on the anti-rotational washer against the flat part of the nut. (5) Install the baggage door panel to the baggage door. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What is the proper method for installing and securing the anti-rotational washer during baggage door lock assembly reinstallation?
answer: Baggage Door Lock Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the baggage door panel to get access to the lock assembly of the baggage door. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices. (2) Remove the 0.75-inch hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. (3) Remove the lock assembly from the door.Baggage Door Lock Assembly Installation . (1) Put the baggage door lock assembly in position on the baggage door. (2) Install the 0.75-inch hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. Make sure that the anti-rotational washer is installed under the 0.75-inch hex nut. (3) Torque the nut. (4) Bend the applicable tab on the anti-rotational washer against the flat part of the nut. (5) Install the baggage door panel to the baggage door. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the detailed procedures for removing and installing the cabin door latch lock components as specified in the instructions?
answer: Cabin Door Latch Lock Removal . (1)  Remove the cam from the latching side of the locking arm. (2)  Remove the washers between the cam and the locking arm. (3)  Remove the locking arm pin from the locking arm and the catch base assembly.Cabin Door Latch Lock Installation . (1) Assemble the locking arm with the locking arm pin. Put one washer on each side of the locking arm. (b) Swage the locking arm pin so there is minimum movement between the parts. (c) Cut the unwanted material from the pin. Put the locking arm pin into the 0.125 inch  diameter hole at the catch base assembly. Align the hole in the locking arm with the hole in the latch base assembly and install the pin. Put three washers between the cam and the locking arm. (5) Attach the cam to the latch side of the locking arm.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the detailed steps involved in removing and reinstalling the cabin door lock assembly as specified in the maintenance procedures?
answer: Cabin Door Lock Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the lower door accent panel and main door panel to get access to the cabin door lock assembly. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices. (2) Remove the armrest door plugs, door panel insert, armrest, door handle, and cover plate from the door to get access to the cabin door lock assembly. (3) Remove the cotter pin, washer, locking arm, and spacer from the lock assembly. (4)  Remove the hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. (5) Remove the lock assembly from the door.Cabin Door Lock Assembly Installation . (1) Put the cabin door lock assembly in position on the cabin door. (2) Install the hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. Install the anti-rotational washer under the hex nut. (3) Torque the nut. (4)  Bend the applicable tab on the anti-rotational washer against the flat part of the nut. (5) Install the spacer, locking arm, washer, and cotter pin that connect the lock assembly to the door handle. (6) Bend the applicable tabs on the cam-pin assembly to make sure that they do not touch the latch housing. (7) Install the armrest door plugs, door panel insert, armrest, door handle, and cover plate. (8) Install the lower door accent panel and main door panel. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices.

question: What are the detailed procedures for attaching the latch base to the door skin and ensuring proper hole alignment during cabin door latch assembly installation?
answer: Cabin Door Latch Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the cabin door lock assembly.  Refer to Cabin Door Lock Assembly Removal/ Installation. (2) Remove the rivets that attach the latch base to the door skin. (4) Remove the pushrod and bolt. (5) Pull the latch handle through the cutout in the door skin. (6)  Remove the latch assembly from the airplane.Cabin Door Latch Assembly Installation . (1) Put the latch assembly in the closed position between the door pan and the door skin. (2)  Make sure the cable assembly is forward of the latch base attach plate, and inboard of latch base cup. (3) Extend the latch handle through the cutout in the door skin. (4)  Push the latch assembly aft so the bolt and pushrod extend through their related holes. (5) Release the pushrod so the bolt is fully extended and the handle is flush. (6) Attach the latch to the door pan with the screws through the base assembly and through the aft flange of the door pan. (7) Make sure the door skin dimension around the latch assembly is correct. CAUTION: Do not make the holes oversize in the latch base. (8)  Drill eleven 0.128 inch  diameter holes that align with the latch base. (9) Make sure the cabin door latch cable assembly rigging and the cabin door inside handle rigging is done before the latch base is attached to the skin. Refer to Cabin Door Latch Cable Assembly Adjustment/Test and Cabin Door Inside Handle Rigging.  Attach the latch base to the door skin with rivets. Install the cabin door lock assembly. question: How can you verify that the baggage door weatherstrip maintains proper seal tension during inspection?
answer: Do an Inspection of the Baggage Door Weatherstrip. (1) Put a 4-inch by 1 1-inch piece of paper between the baggage door frame and the baggage door. Close the baggage door. Slowly pull on the paper to make sure there is seal tension. Move the paper around the perimeter of the door to test the door seal tension. (2) Remove the paper from the door frame. Make sure that the baggage door is closed. Pour a gallon of water over the door and tailcone door frame. After the water no longer drips, open the door and inspect for leaks. (3) If you find a leak, towel dry the upholstery with a clean, dry towel. Install the weatherstrip again as necessary to make sure that there are no leaks around the seal area of the baggage door.Baggage Door Lock Assembly Removal . question: What steps should be followed to verify that the cabin door latch assembly is properly adjusted and functioning correctly after installation?
answer: Do the adjustment of the latch assembly. . (1) Make sure the cabin door is installed and fitted to the fuselage before the adjustment/test can be done. (2) Make sure the cabin door latch is in the OPEN position before the adjustment/test can be done. (3) Make sure the door latch operates smoothly and freely. (4)  Make sure the bolt or pull bar are not filed, ground, or sanded in any way. NOTE:  A noise can be heard when the inside handle is pushed down. It is recommended that the outside door handle be flush with the door skin, although the noise is heard. (5) Install shims to adjust the striker plate forward to give a minimal clearance between the bolt and the striker plate. NOTE:  This adjustment will make sure that the pushrod will engage the latch catch. It will also make sure the exterior handle will stay open until the door is closed again when the door is opened from the outside. (6) Install shims as necessary below the actuator on the cover assembly. NOTE:  If the cabin door is too far forward, the door latch will not operate correctly because the latch assembly pushrod will not cause the bolt to move. (7) Close the cabin door from inside the airplane. (8) Make sure the exterior handle is flush with the door skin when you close the door. (a) If the exterior handle is not flush with the door skin when the door is closed, adjust the push-pull rod out. 1  Remove the screws and the nuts that attach the base plate to the door. 2  Remove the smaller end of the push-pull rod and turn it 180 degrees. 3  Install the screws and nuts that attach the base plate. (9) Do a check for slippage between the cable casing and the clamps that attach the cable.  Install the cotter pin in the clevis pin.

answer: Do the Cabin Door Inside Handle Rigging . (1) Attach the pushrod assembly to the pull bar and attach it with the pin while the latch is attached to the door pan. (2)  Do not install the cotter pin. (3)  Make sure the latch is in the closed position. (4)  Remove the pin that connects the push-pull rod to the latch base assembly. (5) Adjust the rod so a load of 6 to 12 pounds  is necessary at the end of the inner handle to move it from the closed position to the over center position. NOTE:  The rod can be turned in or out 180 degree to make the applicable adjustments. NOTE:  The rod must be attached to the latch assembly before the cabin door inside handle rigging can be done.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What is the recommended approach for preventing overstretching the weatherstrip when installing it around the door corners?
answer: Cabin Door Weatherstrip Removal . (1)  Use a nonmetallic scraper to remove the weatherstrip and adhesive from the door assembly. (2)  Use solvent to remove all remaining adhesive from the door surface.Cabin Door Weatherstrip Installation . (1)  Cut the new weatherstrip to the correct length with the used weatherstrip as a template. (2)  Cut a small notch in the butt ends of the new weatherstrip to let water drain. question: What are the detailed steps to remove and reinstall a baggage door while ensuring its proper operation?

answer: Cabin Door Latch Lock Removal . (1)  Remove the cam from the latching side of the locking arm. (2)  Remove the washers between the cam and the locking arm. question: What are the steps involved in removing and installing the cabin door lock assembly as described in the maintenance procedures?

(6) Bend the applicable tabs on the cam-pin assembly to make sure that they do not touch the latch housing. (7) Install the armrest door plugs, door panel insert, armrest, door handle, and cover plate. (8) Install the lower door accent panel and main door panel. title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the necessary steps to verify that the cabin door latch assembly is correctly positioned and operates smoothly after making adjustments?
answer: Do the adjustment of the latch assembly. . (1) Make sure the cabin door is installed and fitted to the fuselage before the adjustment/test can be done. (2) Make sure the cabin door latch is in the OPEN position before the adjustment/test can be done. (3) Make sure the door latch operates smoothly and freely. (4)  Make sure the bolt or pull bar are not filed, ground, or sanded in any way. NOTE:  A noise can be heard when the inside handle is pushed down. It is recommended that the outside door handle be flush with the door skin, although the noise is heard. (5) Install shims to adjust the striker plate forward to give a minimal clearance between the bolt and the striker plate. NOTE:  This adjustment will make sure that the pushrod will engage the latch catch. It will also make sure the exterior handle will stay open until the door is closed again when the door is opened from the outside. (6) Install shims as necessary below the actuator on the cover assembly. NOTE:  If the cabin door is too far forward, the door latch will not operate correctly because the latch assembly pushrod will not cause the bolt to move. (7) Close the cabin door from inside the airplane. (8) Make sure the exterior handle is flush with the door skin when you close the door. (a) If the exterior handle is not flush with the door skin when the door is closed, adjust the push-pull rod out. 1  Remove the screws and the nuts that attach the base plate to the door. 2  Remove the smaller end of the push-pull rod and turn it 180 degrees. 3  Install the screws and nuts that attach the base plate. (9) Do a check for slippage between the cable casing and the clamps that attach the cable.  Install the cotter pin in the clevis pin.

question: What procedures are recommended to confirm that the baggage door weatherstrip is properly installed and effectively preventing leaks?
answer: BAGGAGE DOOR - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES 1.GeneralA baggage door is installed on the left side of the airplane, aft of the cabin door. The baggage door allows access into the baggage area and into the tailcone. 3 B. A rubber weatherstrip is cemented around the edge of the doorsill.An optional Medeco lock is installed on the baggage door on some airplanes. Baggage Door Removal/installationBaggage Door Removal . (1) Open the baggage door. (2) Disconnect the doorstop chain. (3) Remove the upholstery panel from the door. (4) Remove the bolts that attach the door to the hinges.Baggage Door Installation . (1) Put the baggage door in position on the hinges and attach it with the bolts. (2) Install the upholstery panel to the door. (3) Connect the door stop chain. (4) Close the baggage door and do a check for smooth operation. Baggage Door Weatherstrip Removal/installationBaggage Door Weatherstrip Removal . (2) With a nonmetallic scraper, remove the seal and its adhesive from the doorsill. Remove the adhesive residue and clean the doorsill area with DeSocleanl110Solvent.Baggage Door Weatherstrip Installation . (1) Use the old seal or the doorsill area as a guide to measure and cut the new seal to length. (2) Apply a thin, even coat of EC1300L Adhesive around the circumference of the doorsill area. (3) Make sure that you put the seam at the bottom center of the doorsill. (5) Press the new seal into the adhesive. Allow the adhesive to cure per the manufacturer's instructions, and make sure that the seal completely adheres to the doorsill with no gaps between the seal and the doorsill. (6) Install the baggage door. Baggage Door Weatherstrip InspectionDo an Inspection of the Baggage Door Weatherstrip. (1) Put a 4-inch by 1 1-inch piece of paper between the baggage door frame and the baggage door. Close the baggage door. Slowly pull on the paper to make sure there is seal tension. question: What are the key steps involved in removing and installing the cabin door latch assembly on an aircraft?
answer: Cabin Door Latch Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the cabin door lock assembly.  Refer to Cabin Door Lock Assembly Removal/ Installation. title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What is the recommended method for verifying that the baggage door weatherstrip maintains a proper seal and prevents leaks after installation?
answer: BAGGAGE DOOR - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES 1.GeneralA baggage door is installed on the left side of the airplane, aft of the cabin door. The baggage door allows access into the baggage area and into the tailcone. 3 B. A rubber weatherstrip is cemented around the edge of the doorsill.An optional Medeco lock is installed on the baggage door on some airplanes. Baggage Door Removal/installationBaggage Door Removal . (1) Open the baggage door. (2) Disconnect the doorstop chain. (3) Remove the upholstery panel from the door. (4) Remove the bolts that attach the door to the hinges.Baggage Door Installation . (1) Put the baggage door in position on the hinges and attach it with the bolts. (2) Install the upholstery panel to the door. (3) Connect the door stop chain. (4) Close the baggage door and do a check for smooth operation. Baggage Door Weatherstrip Removal/installationBaggage Door Weatherstrip Removal . (2) With a nonmetallic scraper, remove the seal and its adhesive from the doorsill. Remove the adhesive residue and clean the doorsill area with DeSocleanl110Solvent.Baggage Door Weatherstrip Installation . (1) Use the old seal or the doorsill area as a guide to measure and cut the new seal to length. (2) Apply a thin, even coat of EC1300L Adhesive around the circumference of the doorsill area. (3) Make sure that you put the seam at the bottom center of the doorsill. (5) Press the new seal into the adhesive. Allow the adhesive to cure per the manufacturer's instructions, and make sure that the seal completely adheres to the doorsill with no gaps between the seal and the doorsill. (6) Install the baggage door. Baggage Door Weatherstrip InspectionDo an Inspection of the Baggage Door Weatherstrip. (1) Put a 4-inch by 1 1-inch piece of paper between the baggage door frame and the baggage door. Close the baggage door. Slowly pull on the paper to make sure there is seal tension. Move the paper around the perimeter of the door to test the door seal tension. (2) Remove the paper from the door frame. Make sure that the baggage door is closed. Pour a gallon of water over the door and tailcone door frame. After the water no longer drips, open the door and inspect for leaks. (3) If you find a leak, towel dry the upholstery with a clean, dry towel. Install the weatherstrip again as necessary to make sure that there are no leaks around the seal area of the baggage door.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What steps should be taken to verify that the cabin door latch operates smoothly and without binding after completing the cable assembly rigging?
answer: Do the Cabin Door Latch Cable Assembly Rigging . Attach the clamp and the nut to the cable so it aligns with the 0.193 inch  diameter hole Make sure the door latch is open. title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the specific steps to ensure the cabin door latch assembly is correctly adjusted for proper engagement and smooth operation after installation?
answer: Do the adjustment of the latch assembly. . (1) Make sure the cabin door is installed and fitted to the fuselage before the adjustment/test can be done. (4)  Make sure the bolt or pull bar are not filed, ground, or sanded in any way. NOTE:  A noise can be heard when the inside handle is pushed down. (6) Install shims as necessary below the actuator on the cover assembly. NOTE:  If the cabin door is too far forward, the door latch will not operate correctly because the latch assembly pushrod will not cause the bolt to move. (7) Close the cabin door from inside the airplane. (8) Make sure the exterior handle is flush with the door skin when you close the door. (a) If the exterior handle is not flush with the door skin when the door is closed, adjust the push-pull rod out. 1  Remove the screws and the nuts that attach the base plate to the door. 2  Remove the smaller end of the push-pull rod and turn it 180 degrees. 3  Install the screws and nuts that attach the base plate. (9) Do a check for slippage between the cable casing and the clamps that attach the cable.  Install the cotter pin in the clevis pin.

question: What are the key steps involved in installing a new baggage door weatherstrip to ensure a proper seal on the aircraft?
answer: BAGGAGE DOOR - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES 1.GeneralA baggage door is installed on the left side of the airplane, aft of the cabin door. The baggage door allows access into the baggage area and into the tailcone. 3 B. A rubber weatherstrip is cemented around the edge of the doorsill.An optional Medeco lock is installed on the baggage door on some airplanes. Baggage Door Removal/installationBaggage Door Removal . (1) Open the baggage door. (2) Disconnect the doorstop chain. (3) Remove the upholstery panel from the door. (4) Remove the bolts that attach the door to the hinges.Baggage Door Installation . (1) Put the baggage door in position on the hinges and attach it with the bolts. (2) Install the upholstery panel to the door. (3) Connect the door stop chain. (4) Close the baggage door and do a check for smooth operation. Baggage Door Weatherstrip Removal/installationBaggage Door Weatherstrip Removal . (2) With a nonmetallic scraper, remove the seal and its adhesive from the doorsill. Remove the adhesive residue and clean the doorsill area with DeSocleanl110Solvent.Baggage Door Weatherstrip Installation . (1) Use the old seal or the doorsill area as a guide to measure and cut the new seal to length. (2) Apply a thin, even coat of EC1300L Adhesive around the circumference of the doorsill area. (3) Make sure that you put the seam at the bottom center of the doorsill. (5) Press the new seal into the adhesive. Allow the adhesive to cure per the manufacturer's instructions, and make sure that the seal completely adheres to the doorsill with no gaps between the seal and the doorsill. (6) Install the baggage door. Baggage Door Weatherstrip InspectionDo an Inspection of the Baggage Door Weatherstrip. (1) Put a 4-inch by 1 1-inch piece of paper between the baggage door frame and the baggage door. Close the baggage door. Slowly pull on the paper to make sure there is seal tension. Move the paper around the perimeter of the door to test the door seal tension. (2) Remove the paper from the door frame. Make sure that the baggage door is closed. Pour a gallon of water over the door and tailcone door frame. After the water no longer drips, open the door and inspect for leaks. (3) If you find a leak, towel dry the upholstery with a clean, dry towel. Install the weatherstrip again as necessary to make sure that there are no leaks around the seal area of the baggage door.

answer: Baggage Door Weatherstrip Removal . (2) With a nonmetallic scraper, remove the seal and its adhesive from the doorsill. title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What steps are involved in verifying the proper installation and leak prevention of the baggage door weatherstrip after conducting water testing?
answer: Do an Inspection of the Baggage Door Weatherstrip. (1) Put a 4-inch by 1 1-inch piece of paper between the baggage door frame and the baggage door. Close the baggage door. Slowly pull on the paper to make sure there is seal tension. Move the paper around the perimeter of the door to test the door seal tension. (2) Remove the paper from the door frame. Make sure that the baggage door is closed. Pour a gallon of water over the door and tailcone door frame. After the water no longer drips, open the door and inspect for leaks. (3) If you find a leak, towel dry the upholstery with a clean, dry towel. Install the weatherstrip again as necessary to make sure that there are no leaks around the seal area of the baggage door.Baggage Door Lock Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the baggage door panel to get access to the lock assembly of the baggage door. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices. (2) Remove the 0.75-inch hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. (3) Remove the lock assembly from the door.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the specific steps involved in positioning and securing the cabin door latch assembly during installation to ensure proper function and alignment?
answer: Cabin Door Latch Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the cabin door lock assembly.  Refer to Cabin Door Lock Assembly Removal/ Installation. (2) Remove the rivets that attach the latch base to the door skin. (4) Remove the pushrod and bolt. (5) Pull the latch handle through the cutout in the door skin. (6)  Remove the latch assembly from the airplane.Cabin Door Latch Assembly Installation . (1) Put the latch assembly in the closed position between the door pan and the door skin. (2)  Make sure the cable assembly is forward of the latch base attach plate, and inboard of latch base cup. (3) Extend the latch handle through the cutout in the door skin. (4)  Push the latch assembly aft so the bolt and pushrod extend through their related holes. (5) Release the pushrod so the bolt is fully extended and the handle is flush. (6) Attach the latch to the door pan with the screws through the base assembly and through the aft flange of the door pan. (7) Make sure the door skin dimension around the latch assembly is correct. CAUTION: Do not make the holes oversize in the latch base. (8)  Drill eleven 0.128 inch  diameter holes that align with the latch base. (9) Make sure the cabin door latch cable assembly rigging and the cabin door inside handle rigging is done before the latch base is attached to the skin. Refer to Cabin Door Latch Cable Assembly Adjustment/Test and Cabin Door Inside Handle Rigging.  Attach the latch base to the door skin with rivets. Install the cabin door lock assembly. Refer to Cabin Door Lock Assembly Removal/Installation.

question: What is the correct procedure for adjusting the push-pull rod to ensure that a load of 6 to 12 pounds is required at the inner handle to move the cabin door from the closed to the over-center position during inside handle rigging?
answer: Do the Cabin Door Inside Handle Rigging . (1) Attach the pushrod assembly to the pull bar and attach it with the pin while the latch is attached to the door pan. (2)  Do not install the cotter pin. (3)  Make sure the latch is in the closed position. (4)  Remove the pin that connects the push-pull rod to the latch base assembly. (5) Adjust the rod so a load of 6 to 12 pounds  is necessary at the end of the inner handle to move it from the closed position to the over center position. NOTE:  The rod can be turned in or out 180 degree to make the applicable adjustments. NOTE:  The rod must be attached to the latch assembly before the cabin door inside handle rigging can be done.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What is the purpose of applying a thin layer of adhesive and allowing it to become tacky before pressing the weatherstrip into place during installation?
answer: Cabin Door Weatherstrip Removal . (1)  Use a nonmetallic scraper to remove the weatherstrip and adhesive from the door assembly. (2)  Use solvent to remove all remaining adhesive from the door surface.Cabin Door Weatherstrip Installation . (1)  Cut the new weatherstrip to the correct length with the used weatherstrip as a template. (2)  Cut a small notch in the butt ends of the new weatherstrip to let water drain. (3)  Put the weatherstrip in position with the notches at the door low point. (4)  Apply a thin, smooth layer of EC-1300L, or equivalent adhesive to the two surfaces. (5)  Let the adhesive dry until it is tacky. (6)  Push the weatherstrip in position. (7)  Do not stretch the weatherstrip around the door corners.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What procedures are recommended to adjust the striker plate and pushrod to ensure proper engagement and operation of the cabin door latch?
answer: Do the adjustment of the latch assembly. . (1) Make sure the cabin door is installed and fitted to the fuselage before the adjustment/test can be done. (2) Make sure the cabin door latch is in the OPEN position before the adjustment/test can be done. (3) Make sure the door latch operates smoothly and freely. (4)  Make sure the bolt or pull bar are not filed, ground, or sanded in any way. NOTE:  A noise can be heard when the inside handle is pushed down. It is recommended that the outside door handle be flush with the door skin, although the noise is heard. (5) Install shims to adjust the striker plate forward to give a minimal clearance between the bolt and the striker plate. NOTE:  This adjustment will make sure that the pushrod will engage the latch catch. It will also make sure the exterior handle will stay open until the door is closed again when the door is opened from the outside. (6) Install shims as necessary below the actuator on the cover assembly. NOTE:  If the cabin door is too far forward, the door latch will not operate correctly because the latch assembly pushrod will not cause the bolt to move. (7) Close the cabin door from inside the airplane. (8) Make sure the exterior handle is flush with the door skin when you close the door. (a) If the exterior handle is not flush with the door skin when the door is closed, adjust the push-pull rod out. 1  Remove the screws and the nuts that attach the base plate to the door. 2  Remove the smaller end of the push-pull rod and turn it 180 degrees. 3  Install the screws and nuts that attach the base plate. (9) Do a check for slippage between the cable casing and the clamps that attach the cable.  Install the cotter pin in the clevis pin.

question: What is the step-by-step process for removing and reinstalling the cabin door lock assembly as detailed in the maintenance procedures?
answer: Cabin Door Lock Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the lower door accent panel and main door panel to get access to the cabin door lock assembly. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices. (2) Remove the armrest door plugs, door panel insert, armrest, door handle, and cover plate from the door to get access to the cabin door lock assembly. (3) Remove the cotter pin, washer, locking arm, and spacer from the lock assembly. (4)  Remove the hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. (5) Remove the lock assembly from the door.Cabin Door Lock Assembly Installation . (1) Put the cabin door lock assembly in position on the cabin door. (2) Install the hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. Install the anti-rotational washer under the hex nut. (3) Torque the nut. (4)  Bend the applicable tab on the anti-rotational washer against the flat part of the nut. (5) Install the spacer, locking arm, washer, and cotter pin that connect the lock assembly to the door handle. (6) Bend the applicable tabs on the cam-pin assembly to make sure that they do not touch the latch housing. (7) Install the armrest door plugs, door panel insert, armrest, door handle, and cover plate. (8) Install the lower door accent panel and main door panel. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices.

question: What are the critical steps to ensure the cabin door latch assembly is correctly adjusted for proper engagement and operation?
answer: Do the adjustment of the latch assembly. . (1) Make sure the cabin door is installed and fitted to the fuselage before the adjustment/test can be done. (2) Make sure the cabin door latch is in the OPEN position before the adjustment/test can be done. (3) Make sure the door latch operates smoothly and freely. (4)  Make sure the bolt or pull bar are not filed, ground, or sanded in any way. NOTE:  A noise can be heard when the inside handle is pushed down. It is recommended that the outside door handle be flush with the door skin, although the noise is heard. (5) Install shims to adjust the striker plate forward to give a minimal clearance between the bolt and the striker plate. NOTE:  This adjustment will make sure that the pushrod will engage the latch catch. It will also make sure the exterior handle will stay open until the door is closed again when the door is opened from the outside. (6) Install shims as necessary below the actuator on the cover assembly. NOTE:  If the cabin door is too far forward, the door latch will not operate correctly because the latch assembly pushrod will not cause the bolt to move. (7) Close the cabin door from inside the airplane. (8) Make sure the exterior handle is flush with the door skin when you close the door. (a) If the exterior handle is not flush with the door skin when the door is closed, adjust the push-pull rod out. 1  Remove the screws and the nuts that attach the base plate to the door. 2  Remove the smaller end of the push-pull rod and turn it 180 degrees. 3  Install the screws and nuts that attach the base plate. (9) Do a check for slippage between the cable casing and the clamps that attach the cable.  Install the cotter pin in the clevis pin.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What is the step-by-step procedure for removing and reinstalling the cabin door lock assembly, including the necessary access to interior panels and components?
answer: Cabin Door Lock Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the lower door accent panel and main door panel to get access to the cabin door lock assembly. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices. (2) Remove the armrest door plugs, door panel insert at the armrest, armrest, door handle and cover plate from the door to get access to the cabin door lock assembly. (3) Remove the nut and washer. (4)  Remove the cabin door lock assembly.Cabin Door Lock Assembly Installation . (1) Put the cabin door lock assembly in position. (2) Install the washer and nut. (3) Install the armrest door plugs, door panel insert at the armrest, armrest, door handle and cover plate. (4)  Install the lower door accent panel and main door panel. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What steps are necessary to ensure the cable core is properly positioned for the cabin door latch to operate freely after rigging?
answer: Do the Cabin Door Latch Cable Assembly Rigging . Attach the clamp and the nut to the cable so it aligns with the 0.193 inch  diameter hole Make sure the door latch is open. Cut the casing of the cable assembly approximately two inches  from the clamp bolt on Put the core of the cable through the clamp. Pull the core of the cable through the clamp bolt so the pin extends approximately 0.125 inch  from the door pan contour. Cut the core of the cable approximately one inch  forward of the push rod clamp. Attach the two nuts to the push rod clamp bolt. Make sure the latch operates freely. If the latch binds up and will not operate freely, remove the cable core from the clamp and Do a check of the cable for possible adjustments that will make the latch operate correctly.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What procedures are recommended to confirm the proper sealing and leak prevention of the baggage door weatherstrip during inspection?
answer: Do an Inspection of the Baggage Door Weatherstrip. (1) Put a 4-inch by 1 1-inch piece of paper between the baggage door frame and the baggage door. Close the baggage door. Slowly pull on the paper to make sure there is seal tension. Move the paper around the perimeter of the door to test the door seal tension. (2) Remove the paper from the door frame. Make sure that the baggage door is closed. Pour a gallon of water over the door and tailcone door frame. After the water no longer drips, open the door and inspect for leaks. (3) If you find a leak, towel dry the upholstery with a clean, dry towel. Install the weatherstrip again as necessary to make sure that there are no leaks around the seal area of the baggage door.Baggage Door Lock Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the baggage door panel to get access to the lock assembly of the baggage door. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices. (2) Remove the 0.75-inch hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. (3) Remove the lock assembly from the door.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the sequential steps involved in removing and reinstalling the cabin door latch assembly to ensure proper alignment and secure attachment?
answer: Cabin Door Latch Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the cabin door lock assembly.  Refer to Cabin Door Lock Assembly Removal/ Installation. (2) Remove the rivets that attach the latch base to the door skin. (4) Remove the pushrod and bolt. (5) Pull the latch handle through the cutout in the door skin. (6)  Remove the latch assembly from the airplane.Cabin Door Latch Assembly Installation . (1) Put the latch assembly in the closed position between the door pan and the door skin. (2)  Make sure the cable assembly is forward of the latch base attach plate, and inboard of latch base cup. (3) Extend the latch handle through the cutout in the door skin. (4)  Push the latch assembly aft so the bolt and pushrod extend through their related holes. (5) Release the pushrod so the bolt is fully extended and the handle is flush. (6) Attach the latch to the door pan with the screws through the base assembly and through the aft flange of the door pan. (7) Make sure the door skin dimension around the latch assembly is correct. CAUTION: Do not make the holes oversize in the latch base. (8)  Drill eleven 0.128 inch  diameter holes that align with the latch base. (9) Make sure the cabin door latch cable assembly rigging and the cabin door inside handle rigging is done before the latch base is attached to the skin. Refer to Cabin Door Latch Cable Assembly Adjustment/Test and Cabin Door Inside Handle Rigging.  Attach the latch base to the door skin with rivets. Install the cabin door lock assembly. Refer to Cabin Door Lock Assembly Removal/Installation.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: During the cabin door inside handle rigging process, what steps are necessary to ensure the latch is in the closed position and the push-pull rod is properly adjusted to require 6 to 12 pounds of force to move the handle from the closed to the over-center position?
answer: Do the Cabin Door Inside Handle Rigging . (1) Attach the pushrod assembly to the pull bar and attach it with the pin while the latch is attached to the door pan. (2)  Do not install the cotter pin. (3)  Make sure the latch is in the closed position. (4)  Remove the pin that connects the push-pull rod to the latch base assembly. (5) Adjust the rod so a load of 6 to 12 pounds  is necessary at the end of the inner handle to move it from the closed position to the over center position. NOTE:  The rod can be turned in or out 180 degree to make the applicable adjustments. NOTE:  The rod must be attached to the latch assembly before the cabin door inside handle rigging can be done.

answer: Baggage Door Removal . (1) Open the baggage door. (2) Disconnect the doorstop chain. (3) Remove the upholstery panel from the door. (4) Remove the bolts that attach the door to the hinges.Baggage Door Installation . (1) Put the baggage door in position on the hinges and attach it with the bolts. question: What is the proper procedure for adjusting the push-pull rod to require a load of 6 to 12 pounds at the inner handle for moving the cabin door from the closed to the over-center position during inside handle rigging?
answer: Do the Cabin Door Inside Handle Rigging . (1) Attach the pushrod assembly to the pull bar and attach it with the pin while the latch is attached to the door pan. (2)  Do not install the cotter pin. (3)  Make sure the latch is in the closed position. (4)  Remove the pin that connects the push-pull rod to the latch base assembly. (5) Adjust the rod so a load of 6 to 12 pounds  is necessary at the end of the inner handle to move it from the closed position to the over center position. NOTE:  The rod can be turned in or out 180 degree to make the applicable adjustments. NOTE:  The rod must be attached to the latch assembly before the cabin door inside handle rigging can be done.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the recommended steps to verify that the baggage door operates smoothly and correctly after installation?
answer: BAGGAGE DOOR - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES 1.GeneralA baggage door is installed on the left side of the airplane, aft of the cabin door. The baggage door allows access into the baggage area and into the tailcone. 3 B. A rubber weatherstrip is cemented around the edge of the doorsill.An optional Medeco lock is installed on the baggage door on some airplanes. Baggage Door Removal/installationBaggage Door Removal . (1) Open the baggage door. (2) Disconnect the doorstop chain. (3) Remove the upholstery panel from the door. (4) Remove the bolts that attach the door to the hinges.Baggage Door Installation . (1) Put the baggage door in position on the hinges and attach it with the bolts. (2) Install the upholstery panel to the door. (3) Connect the door stop chain. (4) Close the baggage door and do a check for smooth operation. Baggage Door Weatherstrip Removal/installationBaggage Door Weatherstrip Removal . (2) With a nonmetallic scraper, remove the seal and its adhesive from the doorsill. Remove the adhesive residue and clean the doorsill area with DeSocleanl110Solvent.Baggage Door Weatherstrip Installation . (1) Use the old seal or the doorsill area as a guide to measure and cut the new seal to length. (2) Apply a thin, even coat of EC1300L Adhesive around the circumference of the doorsill area. (3) Make sure that you put the seam at the bottom center of the doorsill. (5) Press the new seal into the adhesive. Allow the adhesive to cure per the manufacturer's instructions, and make sure that the seal completely adheres to the doorsill with no gaps between the seal and the doorsill. (6) Install the baggage door. Baggage Door Weatherstrip InspectionDo an Inspection of the Baggage Door Weatherstrip. (1) Put a 4-inch by 1 1-inch piece of paper between the baggage door frame and the baggage door. Close the baggage door. Slowly pull on the paper to make sure there is seal tension. Move the paper around the perimeter of the door to test the door seal tension. (2) Remove the paper from the door frame. Make sure that the baggage door is closed. Pour a gallon of water over the door and tailcone door frame. After the water no longer drips, open the door and inspect for leaks. (3) If you find a leak, towel dry the upholstery with a clean, dry towel. Install the weatherstrip again as necessary to make sure that there are no leaks around the seal area of the baggage door.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the detailed steps involved in removing and installing the baggage door lock assembly, including the procedures for attaching and securing the anti-rotational washer?
answer: Baggage Door Lock Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the baggage door panel to get access to the lock assembly of the baggage door. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices. (2) Remove the 0.75-inch hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. (3) Remove the lock assembly from the door.Baggage Door Lock Assembly Installation . (1) Put the baggage door lock assembly in position on the baggage door. (2) Install the 0.75-inch hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. Make sure that the anti-rotational washer is installed under the 0.75-inch hex nut. (3) Torque the nut. (4) Bend the applicable tab on the anti-rotational washer against the flat part of the nut. (5) Install the baggage door panel to the baggage door. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the necessary steps to verify that the cabin door latch assembly is properly adjusted for correct operation and alignment after completing the installation?
answer: Do the adjustment of the latch assembly. . (1) Make sure the cabin door is installed and fitted to the fuselage before the adjustment/test can be done. (2) Make sure the cabin door latch is in the OPEN position before the adjustment/test can be done. (3) Make sure the door latch operates smoothly and freely. (4)  Make sure the bolt or pull bar are not filed, ground, or sanded in any way. NOTE:  A noise can be heard when the inside handle is pushed down. It is recommended that the outside door handle be flush with the door skin, although the noise is heard. (5) Install shims to adjust the striker plate forward to give a minimal clearance between the bolt and the striker plate. NOTE:  This adjustment will make sure that the pushrod will engage the latch catch. It will also make sure the exterior handle will stay open until the door is closed again when the door is opened from the outside. (6) Install shims as necessary below the actuator on the cover assembly. NOTE:  If the cabin door is too far forward, the door latch will not operate correctly because the latch assembly pushrod will not cause the bolt to move. (7) Close the cabin door from inside the airplane. (8) Make sure the exterior handle is flush with the door skin when you close the door. (a) If the exterior handle is not flush with the door skin when the door is closed, adjust the push-pull rod out. 1  Remove the screws and the nuts that attach the base plate to the door. 2  Remove the smaller end of the push-pull rod and turn it 180 degrees. 3  Install the screws and nuts that attach the base plate. (9) Do a check for slippage between the cable casing and the clamps that attach the cable.  Install the cotter pin in the clevis pin.

question: What method is recommended to verify the seal tension of the baggage door weatherstrip?

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the specific steps to detach and reattach the cabin door lock assembly during maintenance as described in the procedures?
answer: Cabin Door Lock Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the lower door accent panel and main door panel to get access to the cabin door lock assembly. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices. (2) Remove the armrest door plugs, door panel insert, armrest, door handle, and cover plate from the door to get access to the cabin door lock assembly. (3) Remove the cotter pin, washer, locking arm, and spacer from the lock assembly. (4)  Remove the hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. (5) Remove the lock assembly from the door.Cabin Door Lock Assembly Installation . (1) Put the cabin door lock assembly in position on the cabin door. (2) Install the hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. Install the anti-rotational washer under the hex nut. (3) Torque the nut. (4)  Bend the applicable tab on the anti-rotational washer against the flat part of the nut. (5) Install the spacer, locking arm, washer, and cotter pin that connect the lock assembly to the door handle. (6) Bend the applicable tabs on the cam-pin assembly to make sure that they do not touch the latch housing. (7) Install the armrest door plugs, door panel insert, armrest, door handle, and cover plate. (8) Install the lower door accent panel and main door panel. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices.

question: What is the procedure for checking the seal tension and leak integrity of the baggage door weatherstrip?
answer: Do an Inspection of the Baggage Door Weatherstrip. (1) Put a 4-inch by 1 1-inch piece of paper between the baggage door frame and the baggage door. Close the baggage door. Slowly pull on the paper to make sure there is seal tension. Move the paper around the perimeter of the door to test the door seal tension. (2) Remove the paper from the door frame. Make sure that the baggage door is closed. Pour a gallon of water over the door and tailcone door frame. After the water no longer drips, open the door and inspect for leaks. (3) If you find a leak, towel dry the upholstery with a clean, dry towel. Install the weatherstrip again as necessary to make sure that there are no leaks around the seal area of the baggage door.Baggage Door Lock Assembly Removal . title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What steps should be taken to verify that the cabin door latch assembly remains properly engaged and functions smoothly after completing all adjustments?
answer: Do the adjustment of the latch assembly. . (1) Make sure the cabin door is installed and fitted to the fuselage before the adjustment/test can be done. (2) Make sure the cabin door latch is in the OPEN position before the adjustment/test can be done. (3) Make sure the door latch operates smoothly and freely. (4)  Make sure the bolt or pull bar are not filed, ground, or sanded in any way. NOTE:  A noise can be heard when the inside handle is pushed down. It is recommended that the outside door handle be flush with the door skin, although the noise is heard. (5) Install shims to adjust the striker plate forward to give a minimal clearance between the bolt and the striker plate. NOTE:  This adjustment will make sure that the pushrod will engage the latch catch. It will also make sure the exterior handle will stay open until the door is closed again when the door is opened from the outside. (6) Install shims as necessary below the actuator on the cover assembly. NOTE:  If the cabin door is too far forward, the door latch will not operate correctly because the latch assembly pushrod will not cause the bolt to move. (7) Close the cabin door from inside the airplane. (8) Make sure the exterior handle is flush with the door skin when you close the door. (a) If the exterior handle is not flush with the door skin when the door is closed, adjust the push-pull rod out. 1  Remove the screws and the nuts that attach the base plate to the door. 2  Remove the smaller end of the push-pull rod and turn it 180 degrees. 3  Install the screws and nuts that attach the base plate. (9) Do a check for slippage between the cable casing and the clamps that attach the cable.  Install the cotter pin in the clevis pin.

question: What steps should be followed to properly rig the cabin door inside handle, including attaching the pushrod assembly, verifying the latch is in the closed position, and adjusting the push-pull rod to require a load of 6 to 12 pounds for operation?
answer: Do the Cabin Door Inside Handle Rigging . (1) Attach the pushrod assembly to the pull bar and attach it with the pin while the latch is attached to the door pan. (2)  Do not install the cotter pin. (3)  Make sure the latch is in the closed position. (4)  Remove the pin that connects the push-pull rod to the latch base assembly. (5) Adjust the rod so a load of 6 to 12 pounds  is necessary at the end of the inner handle to move it from the closed position to the over center position. NOTE:  The rod can be turned in or out 180 degree to make the applicable adjustments. NOTE:  The rod must be attached to the latch assembly before the cabin door inside handle rigging can be done.

answer: Cabin Door Latch Lock Removal . (1)  Remove the cam from the latching side of the locking arm. (2)  Remove the washers between the cam and the locking arm. (3)  Remove the locking arm pin from the locking arm and the catch base assembly.Cabin Door Latch Lock Installation . (1) Assemble the locking arm with the locking arm pin. Put one washer on each side of the locking arm. (b) Swage the locking arm pin so there is minimum movement between the parts. (c) Cut the unwanted material from the pin. Put the locking arm pin into the 0.125 inch  diameter hole at the catch base assembly. Align the hole in the locking arm with the hole in the latch base assembly and install the pin. Put three washers between the cam and the locking arm. (5) Attach the cam to the latch side of the locking arm.

title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What steps are involved in inspecting the baggage door weatherstrip for proper sealing and leak prevention?
answer: Do an Inspection of the Baggage Door Weatherstrip. (1) Put a 4-inch by 1 1-inch piece of paper between the baggage door frame and the baggage door. Close the baggage door. Slowly pull on the paper to make sure there is seal tension. Move the paper around the perimeter of the door to test the door seal tension. (2) Remove the paper from the door frame. Make sure that the baggage door is closed. Pour a gallon of water over the door and tailcone door frame. After the water no longer drips, open the door and inspect for leaks. (3) If you find a leak, towel dry the upholstery with a clean, dry towel. Install the weatherstrip again as necessary to make sure that there are no leaks around the seal area of the baggage door.Baggage Door Lock Assembly Removal . (1) Remove the baggage door panel to get access to the lock assembly of the baggage door. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices. (2) Remove the 0.75-inch hex nut and the anti-rotational washer that attach the lock tumbler assembly to the door structure and the cam assembly. (3) Remove the lock assembly from the door.

question: What is the correct sequence for attaching and adjusting the pushrod assembly to ensure the cabin door inside handle operates with a force of 6 to 12 pounds required to move it from the closed to the over-center position?
answer: Do the Cabin Door Inside Handle Rigging . (1) Attach the pushrod assembly to the pull bar and attach it with the pin while the latch is attached to the door pan. (2)  Do not install the cotter pin. (3)  Make sure the latch is in the closed position. (4)  Remove the pin that connects the push-pull rod to the latch base assembly. (5) Adjust the rod so a load of 6 to 12 pounds  is necessary at the end of the inner handle to move it from the closed position to the over center position. NOTE:  The rod can be turned in or out 180 degree to make the applicable adjustments. NOTE:  The rod must be attached to the latch assembly before the cabin door inside handle rigging can be done.

(3) Torque the nut. (4)  Bend the applicable tab on the anti-rotational washer against the flat part of the nut. (5) Install the spacer, locking arm, washer, and cotter pin that connect the lock assembly to the door handle. (6) Bend the applicable tabs on the cam-pin assembly to make sure that they do not touch the latch housing. (7) Install the armrest door plugs, door panel insert, armrest, door handle, and cover plate. (8) Install the lower door accent panel and main door panel. title: CABIN DOORS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What specific steps should be taken to ensure the cabin door latch assembly is correctly aligned and functions properly after adjusting the striker plate, pushrod, and handle to prevent issues with engagement and operation?
answer: Do the adjustment of the latch assembly. . (1) Make sure the cabin door is installed and fitted to the fuselage before the adjustment/test can be done. (2) Make sure the cabin door latch is in the OPEN position before the adjustment/test can be done. (3) Make sure the door latch operates smoothly and freely. (4)  Make sure the bolt or pull bar are not filed, ground, or sanded in any way. NOTE:  A noise can be heard when the inside handle is pushed down. It is recommended that the outside door handle be flush with the door skin, although the noise is heard. (5) Install shims to adjust the striker plate forward to give a minimal clearance between the bolt and the striker plate. NOTE:  This adjustment will make sure that the pushrod will engage the latch catch. It will also make sure the exterior handle will stay open until the door is closed again when the door is opened from the outside. (6) Install shims as necessary below the actuator on the cover assembly. NOTE:  If the cabin door is too far forward, the door latch will not operate correctly because the latch assembly pushrod will not cause the bolt to move. (7) Close the cabin door from inside the airplane. (8) Make sure the exterior handle is flush with the door skin when you close the door. (a) If the exterior handle is not flush with the door skin when the door is closed, adjust the push-pull rod out. 1  Remove the screws and the nuts that attach the base plate to the door. 2  Remove the smaller end of the push-pull rod and turn it 180 degrees. 3  Install the screws and nuts that attach the base plate. (9) Do a check for slippage between the cable casing and the clamps that attach the cable.  Install the cotter pin in the clevis pin.

question: What is the proper procedure for attaching and adjusting the pushrod assembly during cabin door inside handle rigging?
